title: This Fish Stayed in the Air for 45 Seconds

scenes.text: A fish once stayed in the air for forty-five seconds.
A Japanese film crew caught it on camera in 2008, beside a ferry near Yakushima Island.
It beat the old record of forty-two seconds, set in the 1920s.
It leaps out, spreads huge fins like wings, and dips its tail in the water to push off again.
A normal glide is about fifty meters.
This one kept flying. For a fish.

description:
A flying fish was filmed gliding through the air for forty-five seconds in 2008, a world record.
It spreads its fins like wings and uses its tail to launch itself again.
What other animal would you want to see fly?
first_comment: Flying fish usually do this to escape predators. Would you leap out of the water if a tuna chased you?
